answer: An agent economy can gate newcomers by social-graph distance: each must arrive through a short endorsement chain from long-standing seed agents, like water reaching an inlet only through a narrow channel. A Sybil operator may mint thousands of accounts, but each cluster sits across a canyon of missing trust links, far from the seeds, so distance decays its voting and earning weight to near zero. Closing the gap is costly: reputable agents must vouch one by one, staking reputation slashed if the newcomer cheats. The quill of accountability is simple: proximity must be earned, not printed.
